title: Unauthenticated Chrome DevTools Protocol published to the LAN by the browser sidecar
evidence: browsercontainer publishes `0.0.0.0:9222` → container `9223` and the material states "raw CDP is also reachable — published 9222 on the host mapping to container 9223 (docker-compose.browsercontainer.yml:53, SANCTIONED at check-ports-loopback.mjs:99)". The Chrome profile holding Podkey's encrypted vault and the browser's authenticated sessions is a named volume intended to persist (docker-compose.browsercontainer.yml:64, :75-76, "never down -v").
failure: any host on the LAN connects to CDP (the protocol has no authentication — inferred from its nature, not stated in the material) and fully drives the browser: reads logged-in sessions, exfiltrates the Podkey vault, and acts as the browser identity. The ADR-2013 gate has blessed the port, so no CI check will ever flag it.
confidence: high (exposure and profile persistence are stated; the "no auth" property of CDP is inferred)
marked_by_authors: no (it is listed as SANCTIONED, not as a risk)

title: The entrypoint re-widens the host Docker socket to world read-write on every boot while isolation is off
evidence: the host socket is bound rw (docker-compose.override.yml:116); with the shipped `[security].role_isolation = false` (agentbox.toml:2543, setup default agentbox.default.toml:1770) the entrypoint "still runs `chmod o+rw` on every boot" (entrypoint-unified.sh:611-613); the material states the socket is the HOST inode and "only a host-side chmod 0660 narrows it" (docker-compose.override.yml:114-116, risk R2); the sudo drop is baked at build time, so isolation cannot even be trialled without a rebuild (flake.nix:4054-4061, system-manifest.js:97-99).
failure: any code executing as devuser — i.e. every agent session — talks to the host Docker daemon, mounts the host filesystem, and becomes host root. Even if an operator narrows the socket, the next container boot re-widens it.
marked_by_authors: yes (Open R2 in AB-06.13; invariant notes in AB-02.24)

title: Persistent arbitrary MCP-server injection through the devuser-writable `.mcp.json` that reconcile deliberately never touches
evidence: the projector's target is `WORKSPACE/.mcp.json`; "a target entry ABSENT from the ledger is treated as bespoke and is never touched, so adopting this revision cannot delete a hand-written server" (project-mcp-servers.mjs:61-64); only ledger-owned names are removed. The harness spawns each entry's `command` with expanded env at session start (AB-09.7). WORKSPACE is chowned to uid 1000 (entrypoint-unified.sh:585-593), so every agent process can write the file.
failure: one compromised or runaway agent appends a stdio server entry running an arbitrary command; the ownership ledger preserves it forever as "bespoke"; every later session — including the operator's tab0 — spawns it. Root `settings.json` hooks are boot-rewritten, but this file is reconciled, not rewritten, so the injection is the one persistence point that survives reboots.
confidence: medium (the ownership rule and writable target are stated; the injection chain is inferred)
marked_by_authors: no (the never-touch rule is presented as an invariant protecting hand-written entries)

title: Any in-container process can forge any `did:nostr` identity and read every key
evidence: `proxyVerifiedPubkey` trusts `X-Agentbox-Pubkey` from any loopback TCP peer (agent-event-auth.js:98-105, :117); the authors state "a process INSIDE the container can still connect over loopback and forge the stamp, the same-UID boundary (TODO-unified X-1)" (agent-event-auth.js:34-39); `resolveAgentDid` shares the rule (action-plane.js:222-233). With role_isolation off, "every agentbox process runs as devuser, so co-resident code can read the agent key and the bridge key alike" (agent-identity.js 0600 files, AB-11.16 divergence; AB-02.12 "not an OS access boundary").
failure: any co-resident process emits agent-events and action-plane dispatches as the operator's DID, poisoning governance attribution and the audit chain, and exfiltrates the sovereign signing keys.
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt, TODO-unified X-1; DIVERGENCE in AB-11.16 and AB-02.12)

title: The host's `~/.claude` is bound read-write into the container, so container compromise rewrites host credentials
evidence: host `~/.claude` is bound rw at `/var/lib/agentbox/host-claude` "for that purpose alone" (docker-compose.override.yml:83-85, :88); the authors mark it Open: "the credential bind stays writable both ways, so a compromised in-container tool could still modify the host's .claude" (AB-06.11; BASELINE-container.md:235, Q43); the merge daemon pushes whichever side has the later `expiresAt` (cred_sync.rs:29-62).
failure: an in-container attacker crafts a credentials document with a later `expiresAt`; cred-sync pushes it to the host; the host's Claude Code sessions are hijacked or their tokens stolen.

title: Mandate revocation is never enforced at the pod: a revoked delegate keeps its WAC grant
evidence: `revokeMandate` only re-signs the record and rewrites the local registry (routes/mandate.js:238-281); "nothing in agentbox removes or rewrites the `.acl`, so a revoked mandate's WAC grant stays in force at the pod until someone replaces it" (AB-11.7 Tension); the revoking event is not even published to a relay (mandate.js:264-269).
failure: the operator revokes a compromised agent's mandate through the documented API, sees `revoked: true`, and the agent continues to read and write the pod's corpus under the old ACL indefinitely — revocation is a registry annotation, not an enforcement act.

title: The backup tool covers exactly one volume: identity keys, pod data and audit state have no backup path
evidence: `cmd_backup` tars `agentbox-ruvector-data` ("always included", agentbox.sh:306-309) plus a `pg_dump`; its manifest carries only `ruvector_data` and `ruvector_pg_dump` flags (agentbox.sh:400-401). No other `_volume_tar` call appears. Yet the estate declares `agentbox-solid-data` (docker-compose.yml:175-182), the external `agentbox-claude-home` volume (docker-compose.override.yml:185-187), `codex-packages` (:200-203) and `browsercontainer-profile` — and ADR-2118 made the claude-home volume the container-owned home whose loss destroys the sovereign identity keys (AB-06.11, AB-11.2).
failure: disk loss or a bad activation wipes every did:nostr identity the pods' ACLs and mandates reference, all solid-pod contents, and the audit/events state; the DIDs can never sign again and the ruvector restore is the only thing that comes back.
confidence: high that only ruvector-data is included (the command flow is explicit); medium (inferred) that this omission is a defect rather than handled by some unstated external backup

title: The privacy filter classifies mutations by method name, so `dispatch`, `claim`, `close`, `del` and `spawnAgent` bypass redaction into an append-only chain
evidence: the mutation set and prefix rule do not classify those methods (privacy-filter.js:283-313); "the events slot's only write, `dispatch`, therefore reaches the hash-chained JSONL log without redaction, whatever the slot policy says. So do beads `claim` and `close`" (AB-04.5 Tension). The chain's verifier treats any later edit as tamper (audit-chain.js:123-126).
failure: identifier- or PII-bearing payloads are written unredacted into a log whose integrity guarantee makes scrubbing impossible without breaking chain verification — the exposure is permanent by construction (permanence inferred from the stated chain semantics).
confidence: high (the gap is marked; the irreversibility is inferred)

title: The execution journal is appendable by any authenticated principal, not only the operator
evidence: `POST /v1/exec/record` is called "operator-gated" (server.js:433) but attaches no `requireOperator` preHandler, unlike mandate routes (mandate.js:311); in hybrid/nip98 modes any NIP-98-verified signer passes `authMiddleware` (auth.js:194-199); the route appends through the journal singleton onto the events-slot hash chain (exec-record.js:128, AB-03.14).
failure: any nostr key holder injects fabricated execution records and provenance envelopes into the audit chain, corrupting D2 traceability; the entries cannot be removed without breaking the chain.

title: The primary `/mgmt` ingress flow may 401 on NIP-98 re-verification, and two panels in the material disagree about it
evidence: the proxy strips `/mgmt/` and forwards the caller's NIP-98 header verbatim (proxy.mjs:304-310, :886-892); the API rebuilds the URL from the stripped path (auth.js:73); `verifyNip98` accepts only an exact or suffix match of the signed `u` tag (nostr-bridge.js:545-546), and "a tag that keeps `/mgmt/` is not a suffix match of the stripped URL, so this path may answer 401. Only a runtime request through `:9096/mgmt/` can settle it" (AB-03.15 Open). Yet AB-10.7's end-to-end diagram draws the same nip98-passthrough reaching the handler with no failure branch.
failure: if the suffix reading holds, every direct-NIP-98 operator call through the one LAN door — mandate creation, system view — fails 401, pushing operators to the break-glass bearer; the documented write path (AB-03.15's own panel) is dead in production.
confidence: medium (the authors themselves could not settle it from source)
marked_by_authors: yes (Open, AB-03.15) — but the contradiction with AB-10.7's diagram is unmarked

title: bootstrap-seal has a 120 s budget but a 300 s projection wait inside it: slow boots wedge readiness permanently
evidence: the program carries "timeout 120s" (flake.nix:2676) and its status poll runs "up to BOOTSTRAP_SEAL_TIMEOUT=120s" (seal-bootstrap.sh:96-115); `_check_projections` then polls each promised file "up to 300 s" (seal-bootstrap.sh:137) before the sentinel is written (:181). The hub's own bounded wait is 120 s (hub/mod.rs:259). Activation treats /ready failure after 60×2 s as activation failure (runtime-delivery.cjs:267-268).
failure: a legitimate slow boot (programs slow to RUNNING, or the hub projection late) overruns the seal's budget; the sentinel is never written; /ready returns 503 forever while every service is actually up; compose reports unhealthy and every subsequent activation times out — a total operational wedge requiring manual intervention.
confidence: medium (both numbers are stated; which scope the 120 s timeout governs is not)

title: `system-one-proxy` is catalogued boot-class but gated as rebuild-class in the flake, and its absence fails open
evidence: the catalogue entry is `apply_class: boot` (system-manifest.js:274-276, AB-05.13 C13), yet the package set and the supervisor block are both emitted under `lib.optionals`/`lib.optionalString` on `system_one.enabled` (flake.nix:1884, :2134, :3037; AB-02.6 SO1) — exactly the pattern ADR-039's honesty rule reserves for rebuild-class (AB-05.4). confidence: high on the classification contradiction; medium on the operator scenario

title: strict-nip98 auto-elevation silently kills the proxy's bearer_env path used by every browser session
evidence: hybrid "AUTO-ELEVATES to strict-nip98 when AGENTBOX_SOVEREIGN_MESH_ENABLED is true and no mode is set explicitly, and strict-nip98 rejects Bearer unconditionally" (auth.js:172-182, :194-195); the proxy injects `Bearer route.bearer` whenever auth.mode is not nip98 — i.e. for every NIP-07 cookie session and break-glass user (proxy.mjs:893-894); the voice console's Caddyfile routes `/approvals`, `/mgmt`, `/dream` and friends through exactly this proxy (voice/console/Caddyfile:55-106).

title: `agentbox.sh health` exit code is wrong on three paths, in both directions
evidence: `--json` prints the payload and exits 0 unconditionally (agentbox.sh:1148-1151); without jq it prints raw and "falls off the end with status 0" even when slots are degraded (agentbox.sh:1220-1223); exit 1 is reachable only on the pretty path (agentbox.sh:1217-1218). Separately, the exit condition includes `speech_failed` from unconditional curls to ports 8897/8898 (agentbox.sh:1203-1215), "independent of the [adapters] manifest", while the speech pair is its own compose overlay that a deployment may not run (docker-compose.speech.yml).
failure: monitoring that pipes `health --json` never sees degradation (silent incident); conversely, any host without the speech sidecars has health exit 1 permanently, training operators to ignore the alarm. Both failure modes are silent in opposite directions.

evidence: the AB-04.5 Tension ("the events slot's only write, `dispatch`, reaches the hash-chained JSONL log without redaction, whatever the slot policy says"); `privacy-filter.js:283-313`, `:661-663`, `:677-682`; `local-jsonl.js:61`, `:114`; `audit-chain.js:6`, `:68-72`.

title: `POST /v1/exec/record` is described as operator-gated but carries no operator gate
evidence: the mount comment says "operator-gated" (`server.js:433`, `routes/exec-record.js:6-7`), but the route attaches no `requireOperator` preHandler, unlike `routes/mandate.js:311`; in `hybrid`/`nip98` modes any NIP-98-verified signer passes `authMiddleware` (`middleware/auth.js:194-199`), and the route appends through the chain-writing singleton (`routes/exec-record.js:128`).

title: `role_isolation` apply-class drift: the governing doc says boot, the catalogue and image say rebuild
evidence: `BASELINE-container.md:77` calls it boot-class; the catalogue entry is `apply_class: 'rebuild'` (`system-manifest.js:97-99`); the devuser sudo drop is baked from the build-time flag (`flake.nix:4054-4061`), so a boot-time flip reports `degraded:devuser-sudo`; the key's own comment still says "restart to apply" (`agentbox.toml:2536`).
failure: an operator follows the governing doc, flips the flag and restarts, believes the box is isolated; devuser keeps passwordless sudo and the widened socket while every dashboard says the gate is on.

title: In-container loopback forgery of `X-Agentbox-Pubkey`: the stamp authenticates a network position, not a process
evidence: `proxyVerifiedPubkey` accepts the header only from a loopback peer (`agent-event-auth.js:98-105`, `:117`), but any process inside the container can open its own loopback connection (TODO-unified X-1, `agent-event-auth.js:37-39`); `resolveAgentDid` shares the same rule (`action-plane.js:222-233`).
failure: agent-spawned code POSTs to `/v1/agent-events/emit` over loopback behind a session/bearer hop and attributes events to an arbitrary `did:nostr`; audit and governance attribution are forged without a key compromise.

title: Raw CDP published on 0.0.0.0 into a browser whose profile volume holds the Podkey vault
evidence: browsercontainer publishes `0.0.0.0:9222→9223` CDP, sanctioned (`docker-compose.browsercontainer.yml:53`, `check-ports-loopback.mjs:99`); "raw CDP is also reachable" (AB-06.4); the named volume `browsercontainer-profile` holds "Podkey's encrypted vault — never down -v" (`docker-compose.browsercontainer.yml:64`, `:75-76`); `K_browser`'s pubkey is still null and the nip98-proxy roster still admits the house key for it (`config/custody/g5-key-split.json:16-19`, `agentbox.toml:2134`).
failure: a LAN peer connects to CDP (the protocol has no authentication), drives the authenticated browser session and reads the profile/vault — client-site sessions and the still-house-key identity are abused. Inferred composition of stated facts.

title: Break-glass bearer bypasses NIP-98 on the LAN with default-off expiry and scope, and rides query strings on WS
evidence: a single shared bearer is accepted while the secret is set (`proxy.mjs:529-533`, `:567`); the expiry and scope bounds are "both bounds default-OFF and opt-in" (`proxy.mjs:534-544` as drawn; AB-11.16); WS upgrades accept it via `?access_token=`/`?bearer=` (`proxy.mjs:960-965`), a carrier that lands in logs; INGRESS-identity tracks both as known divergences.

title: The bootstrap-done projection table is opt-in: nothing forces a new boot-written file into it
evidence: `_PROJECTIONS` carries two rows today (`seal-bootstrap.sh:141`) and the Open states "nothing forces a new boot-written file into it"; the sentinel is the sole readiness signal (DDD-001), and ADR-2104 documents the exact prior failure — sentinel written over a boot that skipped projections.

title: System One consumers are all-true in the manifest while activation is staged, and the five external consumers get `_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` by default
evidence: ADR-2155 is `accepted`/`complete`/`staged` (`ADR-2155:5-7`) while `[system_one.consumers]` sets all nineteen true (`agentbox.toml:906-927`); the exports for visionflow, website, solid pod, ontomark and vault rank each carry `_ALLOW_CLOUD=1` with no laya endpoint unless listed (`system_one.rs:553-639`); routing prompts ride the proxy with no client-side key (`lib/skill-route.cjs:418`, `:682-684`).
failure: on image activation, prompts and tool content from five external systems egress to the cloud backend by default — a confidentiality incident against a client contract, with no configuration change to blame.
confidence: high for the facts; the harm is inferred
marked_by_authors: yes (Open for the staging; the `_ALLOW_CLOUD` default is stated unmarked in the panel)

title: Unsigned mandates persist and `isMandateActive` never checks a signature
evidence: an entry can sit in `registry.json` with no signed event behind it and `ensureMandate` keeps returning it (`routes/mandate.js:150-153`, `:171`); `isMandateActive` checks only `revoked`/`expires_at` (`lib/mandate.js:191`); a re-mint content-addresses a fresh `issued_at` and produces a new URN rather than signing the old record (`lib/mandate.js:107`, `:113-124`); the registry is a local same-uid-writable file (`routes/mandate.js:52`).
failure: grants minted while the signer was down remain usable forever; in-container tamper re-marks a revoked entry active (compounds with F-03).

title: Pod writes sign under the container's sovereign identity, not the mandate grantee
evidence: the default signer is `loadSovereignSigner` (`pod-signer.js:98-99`); `AGENTBOX_PROFILE` no longer selects a stack (`pod-signer.js:21-26`); the per-session grantee is the profile DID (`routes/sessions-boundary.js:294`).
failure: per-agent mandate grants never bind the writes actually made; everything is attributed to and authorized as the container identity, so profile-level revocation changes nothing at the pod.

title: A caller-supplied `Authorization` header bypasses the pod signer and `requireSigned` in both modes

title: Capability trust classes are validated and reported but consumed by nothing
evidence: declarations are validated (`capability-scope.js:113-114`) and surfaced (`execution-coverage.js:59`), but "neither the authority gate nor the mandate code reads them"; the acknowledged bypasses (code-mode sub-calls, MCP plugins, background jobs) stand.

evidence: the BASELINE's supervised-set table gates `sidestr-producer` on `[sidechain.signer].enabled` (`BASELINE-container.md:403`); the code gates on top-level `[sidechain].enabled` (`flake.nix:322`), shipped true after the ENOSPC recovery (`agentbox.toml:1959`); the `signer`/`bridge` sub-blocks have no schema entry (`BASELINE-container.md:362-363`).

evidence: voicelink `enabled = true`/`record_events = true` (`agentbox.toml:2264`, `:2271`) while ADR-2151 is `proposed`/`none`/`inactive`, baking `voice-paned` (`flake.nix:1848-1850`, `:2129`) and registering hooks (`entrypoint-unified.sh:2165`); jev-compaction enabled (`agentbox.toml:741`) while ADR-2121 is staged with no image booted (`ADR-2121:161-163`); ADR-2155 staged vs consumers all-true; isaac-sim dispatches unconditionally (`agentbox.sh:2891`) with an ungated live catalogue entry (`system-manifest.js:178`) while ADR-2149 is proposed; ADR-2154 staged while the Pele probe already runs (`artifact-probes.json:75-78`).

title: Health signals that cannot fail: the adapter gauge is never set and the CLI exits 0 on degraded output
evidence: `agentbox_adapter_health` is declared (`metrics.js:35-40`) with a setter that has no caller (`metrics.js:202-204`) while BASELINE claims it is surfaced (`BASELINE-container.md:119`); `agentbox.sh health --json` prints and exits 0 regardless (`agentbox.sh:1148-1151`); a host without `jq` returns 0 even when slots are degraded (`agentbox.sh:1220-1223`).

title: Default relay consumer admits any signed author from public relays into local handlers
evidence: With `ingressPolicy = allowlist`, an empty allowlist ADMITS every signed author (`mcp/nostr-bridge/relay-consumer.js:764-768`) — the opposite of the Rust boundary's deny-all (`services/nostr-pod-bridge/src/admission.rs:35-45`). Nothing in `flake.nix`, the entrypoint or the manifest projector sets `AGENTBOX_RELAY_ALLOWED_PUBKEYS` (`management-api/server.js:1434`). The manifest sets `external_fanout = "bidirectional"` (`agentbox.toml:175` → `flake.nix:4515`), which adds `wss://relay.damus.io,wss://relay.primal.net` (`flake.nix:4321`) to the subscription; any signed author whose event p-tags a local npub (I10) passes I07 into the governance, intent and payment handlers and pod inbox files. The authority gate's own responder allowlist (`management-api/lib/authority-consumer.js:259-271`) keeps 31403 decisions closed, so it is not an approvals bypass — it is ungoverned remote event ingestion into state agents consume.
failure: anyone with a Nostr key publishes a p-tagged event on damus or primal; it lands in `pods/<npub>/events/inbox/` and intent markers, and local agents act on it as if it came from an authorised peer.
marked_by_authors: yes (Tension "JS consumer allowlist" plus an explicit Open on the runtime configuration)

title: Shipped default leaves every role secret, including the break-glass bearer, ambient in every child process
evidence: With `role_isolation = false` (the shipped default), the capture/scrub functions "return at their first line, so every other ROLE variable stays in PID 1 and reaches every child" (`entrypoint-unified.sh:395`, `entrypoint-unified.sh:439`). The break-glass bearer is one of those ROLE variables (`proxy.mjs:53`) and "is still the same value as BRIDGE_TOKEN until Q4" (AB-16.9 C3) — and BRIDGE_TOKEN must be set for the voice loop's container-to-container path. Break-glass matching alone, with unset expiry and unset scope, is a full NIP-98 identity bypass whose downstream attribution is a sentinel placeholder pubkey (AB-16.6). Compounding it, every supervised program runs as `devuser` uid 1000, so "each can read every other's 0600 key file and the mirror key" (AB-16.1 N4) and uid 1000 is admitted to the session socket by design (`session-plane-acl.json:8-11`).
failure: any compromised MCP server, consultant CLI or agent process reads `NIP98_PROXY_ALLOW_BEARER` from its own environment (or any co-resident key file) and authenticates to port 9096 as a full identity bypass over the LAN, with every action attributed to a fake sentinel pubkey.
marked_by_authors: partly — the same-uid divergence is marked (AB-16.1 N4); the PID-1 env reach (AB-16.13) and the bearer-equals-BRIDGE_TOKEN fact (AB-16.9 C3) are stated without markers and their combination is unflagged

evidence: ADR-2041 wired exactly one surface — `POST /v1/tasks` via `dispatchTaskSpawn` (`action-plane.js:254`). title: One shared secret is both the tab0-bridge bearer and the NIP-98 break-glass, rides in URLs, and has no expiry

AB-12.7 — the Unmute backend holds the token as `KYUTAI_LLM_API_KEY` (`voice/README.md:93`). confidence: high that the credential is shared, URL-carried and unbounded by configuration; inferred that a URL/log/voice-container leak is the entry.

title: The agentbox→VisionClaw agent-event pipeline is non-functional in release: wrong envelope shape, no credential, and emitted fields dropped at ingest
evidence: the subscriber forwards the bare publisher event (`agent-event-ws-subscriber.js:144-151`) while the canonical `jsonrpc`/`method`/`params` envelope is built only by `createMcpNotification` (`agent-event-publisher.js:305-343`), which the subscriber never calls; `AgentActionNotification` requires those fields with no serde default (`src/agent_events/schema.rs:26-29`), so `process_frame` returns `Malformed` (`ingest.rs:101,149`) — "no forwarded frame from this path reaches the hub." Independently, the subscriber sends no auth (`agent-event-ws-subscriber.js:94`, `server.js:383`), and a release VisionClaw refuses the upgrade with 401 (`ingest.rs:291-292`). Additionally, `failure_mode` and `authority_class` are emitted (`agent-event-publisher.js:326,335`) but silently parsed away because the Rust mirror lacks the fields and does not deny unknown fields (`schema.rs:60-147`); `intent` (`schema.rs:143`) is never emitted.
failure: in a release deployment the entire cross-container agent-event/beam telemetry feature produces nothing — the socket either never authenticates or accepts and rejects every frame as `malformed_json` — while the publisher reports success (`broadcast_count`) and the subscriber retries on backoff, so the outage is silent and unalerted.
marked_by_authors: yes (Drift ×2 in ES-02.2; Open in ES-02.3)

evidence: VisionClaw embeds crates.io `0.5.0-alpha.17` (`Cargo.toml:246`); agentbox builds the `0.5.0-alpha.18` workspace at rev `76ab7aab` adding `SOLID_POD_JEV_ALLOW_CLOUD` (`solid-pod-rs.nix:54,56-58`); docs cite alpha.9 (`native-pod-mesh.md:3-4`), alpha.13 (`solid-pod.md:37`) and alpha.17 (`BASELINE-container.md:241`).
failure: two divergent pod implementations serve the same protocol; a fix (e.g. the ADR-2008 rust-bitcoin port) present in one is absent in the other; an operator debugging from the docs works against the wrong version.

title: Client pod path computations land data in the wrong places
evidence: `pod_structure` appends the npub to a `pod_base` that already ends in it (`solid_proxy_handler.rs:287-288` called at `:1088,:1174`; bases built `:975,:1155`), so init reports `base/npub/npub/...`; `ensurePublicTypeIndex` cuts at the first `/settings/`, but the caller passes the preferences container, which has no such segment — `indexOf` returns -1 and the Type Index lands at a nine-character prefix (`typeIndex.ts:70-73`; `SolidPodService.ts:447`; `solid_proxy_handler.rs:294`).
failure: preferences and type registrations are written outside their intended containers; the public Type Index is published at a nonsense path; discovery and ACLs point at the wrong resources.

title: A crafted `stale_after` panics the relay's proposal admission path

The section's own business note: "A single success counter does not establish all four."

title: Removing an administrator on the relay leaves their auth-worker admin authority intact; they re-grant themselves
evidence: NF-08.7 N3C labels this "REVOCATION GAP: relay set-admin changes only whitelist (`whitelist.rs:450`); Auth members can retain its grant (`admin.rs:90`)"; N3 records that the 66ca8d8 closure only removed the relay's members query; N4/N5: `ADMIN_PUBKEYS` is declared in no relay/auth template and named in no SETUP step, so an operator has no documented lever to remove static authority either. NF-25.3's fixture "executes the write and both store queries"; "an error in one source is not a denial from the union."
confidence: high — the split is directly evidenced by executed fixture and cited code; that this path fired in the incident is inferred.

title: Preview worker SSRF guard is denylist-only in any by-the-book deploy, with no wall-clock timeout
evidence: the code acknowledges "the Workers runtime exposes no resolve-then-pin primitive, so without PREVIEW_ALLOWED_HOSTS the guard is denylist-only and DNS-rebinding-vulnerable" (`ssrf.rs:13`); the template declares only `ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (`preview-worker/wrangler.toml:13`); "there is NO wall-clock timeout — only redirect-count and body-size limits bound a fetch" (N3).
failure: a member posts a link whose hostname re-binds to an internal address after the first resolve; the per-hop policy re-check sees an innocent hostname while egress hits an internal service; the unfurl renders internal response metadata back to the requester. Separately, a slow-drip origin pins Worker invocations because nothing bounds fetch time.

title: Both clients omit the NIP-98 header registration requires, so passkey signup 401s for everyone
evidence: forum client posts plain JSON (`passkey.rs:173`; `http.rs:156` — Content-Type only, no Authorization); BBS client likewise (`bbs-client/src/passkey.rs:356`); the worker requires a NIP-98 header and matching author (`webauthn.rs:836`, `:849`) and returns 401 before attestation validation.
failure: every passkey registration is rejected with 401; no passkey account can be created on either client; the operator's onboarding funnel for the flagship identity path is dead and support cannot see why (the failure is pre-attestation, so nothing about WebAuthn appears in logs).

title: Registration stores a different PRF salt than it issued, so login can never derive the same identity key
evidence: options issues random salt A (`webauthn.rs:739`); verify ignores the submitted salt and hashes a server secret + credential id + pubkey into B (`webauthn.rs:1021`); login options returns B (`webauthn.rs:1128`); the client derives at registration with A (`passkey.rs:153`) and at login with the returned salt (`passkey.rs:264`). Native controls prove different roots for A/B even with identical PRF output.
failure: the moment the F-02 header defect is repaired (or any other path completes registration), every passkey member who logs out can never log back into the same pubkey — permanent, silent custody loss of every passkey account, with the stranded keys' posts and DMs orphaned.

title: Device-key controls are unusable when they matter: the list parser rejects every populated list, revocation never touches AUTH, and caches outlive the write
evidence: server rows use f64 for `created_at`/`revoked` (`devices.rs:326`) and serialise them (`:470`); the client parser expects u64/u8 and a non-empty server list fails (`utils/devices.rs:264`) — five native contract tests confirm. AUTH stores the raw public key (`nip_handlers.rs:2069`) and persists it (`session.rs:334`); the registry query selects revoked=0 (`nip_handlers.rs:2596`) with "no explicit revoked-key rejection" at `:974`; the auth-worker revoke writes its D1 row with no relay cache invalidation, and owner lookups are cached 60s including negatives (`read_cache.rs:73`); an existing device row can be re-registered to a new owner with revoked reset (`devices.rs:416`) while revoke matches the current owner only (`:511`).
failure: a member loses their phone, opens the device list — it errors precisely because devices exist. Even after a direct revoke, the lost phone's existing authenticated session keeps its raw-key identity (AUTH unaffected), cached viewer contexts keep owner-derived privileges up to 60s, and if the device was re-registered the original owner's revoke matches no row.

title: The search template ships a real default admin pubkey; any deploy that doesn't override grants that key admin of ingest
evidence: `search-worker/wrangler.toml:41` ships a real 64-hex pubkey, "the only non-placeholder value where every other template ships example.com or a zeroed key" (N3); the worker reads it as its only admin source (`auth.rs:54`) and enforces it at ingest (`auth.rs:86`).
failure: an operator deploys by the book; whoever holds that key can POST /ingest, indexing arbitrary labelled "public" content; since the client consults the worker in semantic mode or when relay text search returns nothing (`global_search.rs:336-360`), an unowned party can shape what members find.

title: BBS backup exports the stored forum key, not the active account's key
evidence: backup is offered when `local_secret_hex` returns a value (`screens.rs:1972`), requires only "some active public key" (`signer.rs:291`, `:295`), and reads forum storage with no comparison to the active public key; a generated key is returned once and never updates forum storage (`signer.rs:147`).
failure: forum key A remains stored while local signer B is installed; the member backs up from BBS, exports A while the screen names B, and never writes B down. Storage cleared — account B is unrecoverable. Conversely an in-memory pasted key has no backup route when forum storage is empty.
confidence: high (source-traced condition; browser reproduction remains open per the review)

title: Governance read endpoints are effectively anonymous and the admin-gated reviewer aggregate is reconstructable
evidence: "the governance READ endpoints verify a NIP-98 signature with no membership check, so authenticated is effectively anonymous, and the admin-gated reviewer aggregate can be reconstructed from the un-gated decisions read" (`known-findings.md:23`, `:24`) — an operator decision, taken once for both.
failure: anyone (key generation is free) enumerates all cases and decisions, including moderation-sensitive subjects, and diffs the decisions read over time to reconstruct who reviewed what — reviewer privacy and case-subject confidentiality are unenforceable.

title: Core aggregate guards compare pubkeys case-sensitively while the same key verifiably presents in two casings
evidence: "the self-review and original-signer guards compare pubkeys case-SENSITIVELY while NIP-98 returns the pubkey verbatim" (`known-findings.md:29`); the same key "can legitimately present in two casings and both verify" (`governance_api.rs:98-100`); the registry side already fixed this class via `canonical_agent_pubkey` (`governance_api.rs:108`) — the core aggregate was left open.
failure: a broker mangles its pubkey casing when publishing a 31403; the self-review / original-signer string comparison passes; the broker decides its own case or supersedes another's decision, defeating the ADR-2011 boundary the whole surface rests on.
confidence: high (casing property asserted in the material; the bypass is the direct arithmetic of the two cited facts)

title: After owner resolution, the moderation gates key on the raw signing pubkey; gift wraps have no author to resolve at all
evidence: "the write gate resolves a device key to its owner, but the moderation gates that follow key on the RAW signing pubkey, and a gift wrap has no author to resolve at all" (`known-findings.md:27`, `:44`). Note a conflict to resolve at the code: NF-03.4 step 9 states suspension and silence are "checked for the device key AND its owner" (`nip_handlers.rs:1189`) — the two citations disagree about which gates cover the owner; check the ban/mute call site (`nip_handlers.rs:1213`) before acting.
failure: a banned or muted owner acting through a fresh raw key (or any gift-wrap-shaped path) is evaluated against an identity the moderation state was never recorded for; enforcement meant for the person never lands.
confidence: medium (the defect is recorded; which gates are affected conflicts between citations)

title: The NIP-98 replay store fails open when D1 returns no write metadata
evidence: the store answers first-seen when D1 returns no write metadata (`rate-limit/src/replay.rs:37-39`; the trait contract is `true` on first observation, `core/src/nip98.rs:94-95`); the full signature/URL/method/payload/freshness check runs first (`nip98.rs:576`), bounding exposure to a captured token inside its freshness window.
failure: on any request where D1 omits the metadata, an intercepted admin Authorization header re-submitted within the window passes — e.g. replayed to `/api/governance/agents/register`. Whether D1 ever omits it is runtime behaviour the material says is not settled.

title: ENCRYPTION_ENABLED is declared in no wrangler template, so a forgotten var silently leaves "encrypted" zones in plaintext
evidence: ENCRYPTION_ENABLED is read from env at `zone_config.rs:86` but "declared in NO wrangler.toml [vars] block in any worker — ... it has no documented deployment default, so a deploy that forgets it silently leaves encryption OFF" (N4); `is_encrypted = gate AND zone.encrypted AND NOT is_public_read` (`zone_config.rs:133`); the write-side ciphertext requirement fires only inside that branch (`nip_handlers.rs:1457-1459`); SETUP never names it.
failure: the operator marks a zone encrypted in forum.toml, never sets the relay var because no template or guide mentions it; the relay's encrypted-zone gates never engage, members post into what is labelled a private family zone, and every read-cohort member (and the relay itself, which would otherwise see only ciphertext shape) sees plaintext.

title: Live broadcast of kind-41 skips the zone gate that the history path enforces
evidence: the live `needs_gate` includes kinds 40 and 42 plus calendar and kanban and omits 41 (`broadcast.rs:76`); gated kinds consult the authoriser per recipient (`:149`) but "Kind 41 skips zone context — matching subscription gets original event" (`:162`); the history path withholds a hidden-zone kind 41 from non-members (`nip_handlers.rs:2354`); the native dispatcher test sends kind 41 despite a fixture authoriser that would withhold.
failure: any connected socket holding a kind-41 subscription receives channel metadata edits for hidden zones in real time — the zone's existence and name leak live even though a later REQ for the same history would be withheld.
confidence: high (dispatcher-level evidence; no live relay probe was run)

title: Invite revocation can never succeed: the client sends the code, the handler matches the id
evidence: creation uses an 8-character id and a 16-character code (`invites.rs:361`); the client puts the code in the revoke URL (`admin/invites.rs:175`); the handler looks up `WHERE id = input` (`invites.rs:733`) and returns 404 "Invite not found" (`:742`); the SQL fixture misses by code and succeeds by id.
failure: a leaked invite code cannot be withdrawn — every revoke attempt 404s and the invite stays redeemable; for a zone invite, redemption also grants zone cohorts on the relay whitelist (`invites.rs:230`, `:245`, `:271`).

title: Member deletion reports "Deleted" after partial cleanup, leaves no tombstone, and the row can be silently re-granted
evidence: relay deletion must succeed but pod deprovision and auth member cleanup failures only log warnings (`admin/mod.rs:506`, `:524`); the UI reports Deleted (`:533`); the whitelist DELETE leaves "no removed-state tombstone" (`user_admin.rs:199`); the storage fixture can grant a new row after deletion.
failure: a removed member's pod data and auth row survive; because there is no tombstone, any later cohort grant or zone-invite path re-creates the whitelist row for the same pubkey (the shared merge preserves cohorts), quietly re-admitting a person the operator removed, whose pod content was never deprovisioned.

title: Zone-key delivery permanently skips members whose newest-epoch grant landed but older epochs were lost; stale writers fork readability
evidence: auto-grant includes missing older epochs only for recipients lacking a newest-epoch ACK (`auto_grant.rs:94`, `:102`); publish returns without waiting for a relay ACK (`relay.rs:640`); a positive ACK records the key while a negative ACK changes nothing (`auto_grant.rs:153`), and the next sweep filters on the same newest-ACK and skips the recipient entirely (`:100`). Rotation has "no shared epoch activation barrier" (`zone_encryption.rs:273`); a stale writer encrypts with the locally supplied older key (`store.rs:359`, `mod.rs:568`) while the relay checks shape only (`zone_config.rs:208`).
failure: a member's newest-epoch grant is ACKed but an older-epoch grant is lost in delivery; every later sweep skips them, so they can never read pre-rotation history and no error ever surfaces. In parallel, a stale-writer admin posts new ciphertext under the old epoch that newest-only members cannot decrypt — the encrypted zone silently splits into two readable halves.
confidence: high (scheduling and filter logic cited; the production occurrence is inferred)

title: The legacy VisionClaw pipeline still publishes with a fail-open redactor and an unscanned frontmatter channel
evidence: OM-00.3 EXT states "VisionClaw's vault build job still ships S1.1, S1.2, S1.5, S2.3 and S3.1 unchanged until VC-60 retires under its four gates" (ADR-OM-005-estate-alignment...md:28). S1.1 is "prose redactor failed OPEN on a regex compile error" and S1.2 is "credential scan was body-only but render publishes frontmatter" (OM-00.2 A1, A2). The VisionClaw workflow builds the in-tree `vault` crate, not ontomark (`ontology-publish.yml:167-168`), its output feeds `pack-pod-resources.py` (`ontology-publish.yml:247`), and "the legacy `vault` build kept private links" (OM-05.5). ADR-OM-005 decision 2 retires this job "gated, so it keeps running."

marked_by_authors: yes (EXTERNAL in OM-00.3; EXTERNAL notes in OM-05.5)

evidence: OM-11.2 GAP: "bare private working name can survive in a public knowledge title; knowledge redactor is not the union redactor (projection.rs:750,850,890)". The audit reproduced it: the same private working-note title was masked in a public working title but "retained in a public knowledge title. Both public and machine builds retained the latter." The union marker set is built over both vaults (projection.rs:837-850) but applied only to surviving working records (projection.rs:869-875); the page title is taken from the projected record (page_api.rs:89).

The publication boundary the redactor claims (private names masked) does not hold for titles.

title: Governance application can mutate a page its receipt does not name, and the promote path skips the digest-equality check approve has
evidence: OM-07.1 X: "explicit promote checks request tag, but lacks approve's proposal-digest equality check (local-process-manager.js:444,400)". OM-07.2 GAP: "staged title B can write B.md while adapter receipt names proposal page A (ontology-apply.js:570 vs write/create.rs:258)" — the CLI derives the filename from the staged title (write/create.rs:248,258) and the adapter receipts the original proposal page (ontology-apply.js:634). Ledger attestation failure is returned after the write (ontology-apply.js:742,900).
failure: an approved decision for case X is executed via promote with a proposal whose digest does not match the decision tag; or a create proposal lands as `B.md` while the ledger records page A. Later audit of "which approved change reached which page" is wrong, and nothing in the local flow detects it — the write itself is valid.
marked_by_authors: yes (TENSION in OM-07.1; DRIFT in OM-07.2)

title: The derivation certificate is written outside the bundle transaction: before the consistency gate, deletable by promotion, and orphanable beside an old bundle
evidence: "certificate files are written directly to certificate_out before consistency, no bundle transaction covers them (mod.rs:723-725)" (OM-03.1, marked Tension). OM-10.2: on an unsatisfiable refusal the "old bundle can retain new certificate beside it (mod.rs:744)", and a certificate placed inside the output directory "is removed by successful replacement (mod.rs:311,313,316)". The estate audit "reproduces failures that separate the certificate from the surviving bundle."
failure: a build refuses as unsatisfiable after writing its certificate — disk now holds a warrant for a closure that was never published, beside the previous bundle. Or an operator points `--certificate-out` inside `--out` and every successful promotion destroys the warrant. A verifier cannot tell which certificate covers which bundle.
marked_by_authors: yes (Tension in OM-03.1; TENSION ×2 in OM-10.2)

title: The independent certificate checker accepts an empty derivation file, and the four certificate files are written non-atomically
evidence: the checker receives only the two TSV files (`oo_cert.rs:54,55,56`); "omitting all steps still passes — soundness does not establish closure completeness." Reproduced: the checker "accepted an empty derivation file after a one-step certificate was truncated." `scope.tsv` and `asserted.sha256` are "not inputs to this checker invocation." The writer performs "four sequential filesystem writes (rdfs-certificate/src/lib.rs:589-592)" and "a failed second write can leave new assertions with old digest (589,590)."
failure: truncation or tampering of `derivations.tsv` yields a certificate that still re-verifies; a crash mid-write circulates a set whose digest does not match its assertions. The trust artefact ADR-OM-009 exists to provide is forgeable by omission and corruptible by a torn write, with no consumer-side check covering the metadata files.

title: `publish_out` is written after promote, so a failure leaves two destinations at different generations with no rollback
evidence: OM-03.5 N2: "write_to runs AFTER promote, so a failure there leaves the NEW bundle beside the PREVIOUS publication tree that swap_in kept, the two no longer one generation (build/publish.rs:356, mod.rs:1026-1028)." The report counts both destinations and the CLI only refuses a zero (mod.rs:1050-1057, main.rs:902-908), so a partial write passes.
failure: promote succeeds, the external publication write fails (permissions, disk) — the promoted bundle at `out` is the new generation while the published tree at `publish_out` still serves the previous one. Consumers reading both (visionGraph's `site-data` and `quartz/content`) see mixed generations, and the build reports success-or-generic-error with no restoration of the retired bundle.

title: An ingest rerun deletes and replaces a complete review bundle under the same ID, and "complete" can stay true after dropped chunks
evidence: the request ID determines the default directory and the run first removes the existing manifest directory (`ingest_cmd.rs:769,771,772`); "incomplete uncached rerun can replace complete bundle under same ID (ingest_cmd.rs:723,769,772)" — reproduced by the audit. The endpoint is "omitted from request ID (ingest_cmd.rs:606)" although it is part of the parser and the response cache (`:570,446`). A malformed model response records a dropped chunk only; "complete can remain true (ingest_cmd.rs:821)" and the source is recorded as finished (`:842`). Removed sources are "dropped from host result; only finished observed sources recorded (:841,843)" although the library classifies them (`ledger.rs:224,255`).
failure: a network hiccup on a rerun destroys a previously complete bundle of accepted proposals and evidence quotes; a reviewer trusting the "complete" flag or the bundle ID gets a partial artifact presented as whole, and evidence that was accepted earlier is gone with no record of removal.
marked_by_authors: yes for the replacement and endpoint drift (TENSION/DRIFT, OM-08.3); no marker on the complete-flag-stays-true edge (OM-08.2)

title: ADR-OM-009 says every published closure carries a certificate; the default build writes and checks none, and contract C3 lists no certificate artefact
evidence: the ADR is Accepted and "active from v0.6.0" and "makes ontomark... the writer of the warrant a Lean 4 checker can re-verify" (OM-03.8). Against that: "certificate_out defaults to absent and the build writes and checks nothing then (mod.rs:738, main.rs:410)" — the authors' own Open question. OM-04.1 NC: "the C3 file listing names no certificate output (sovereign-corpus-contracts.md:111), while ADR-OM-009 decides every published closure carries one."

marked_by_authors: yes (Open in OM-03.8; DRIFT in OM-04.1) — the ADR-title contradiction itself is only implied

title: Graph extraction drops unsupported shapes and unreadable definitions before the refusal check, so the published closure can be silently incomplete

Reproduced at the Graph API: a raw universal restriction produced zero refusals, and a malformed graph definition was omitted (OM-10.1 DROP). The material cautions these are "Graph API probes, not a demonstrated bypass of normal vocabulary loading."

The build succeeds, the zero-unsatisfiable gate passes, and consumers receive an incomplete closure with no error, warning, or count.
confidence: medium (reproduced at the adapter boundary; the normal vocabulary-load path is partially guarded by NON_EL checks at load)
marked_by_authors: yes (AUDIT LIMIT in OM-04.3; TENSION in OM-10.1)

evidence: OM-05.1 n2 asserts as INVARIANT that "all means BOTH for validate, gate, conflicts, find and build" (migrate_cmd.rs:64-68; main.rs:663,699,758,914) and in the same note: "DIVERGENCE: retrieve, tree and edit call `.next()` on the loaded vaults, so under all they read knowledge alone (main.rs:936-939,961-964,984-987)."

The same flag means two different scopes depending on the verb, with no error in either.
