title: Relation tables are hardcoded in three emitters, so vocabulary-added relations are declared but never stubbed, never drawn, and unordered
evidence: "the stub list is a hardcoded array of 13 property names (turtle.rs:446-460), a third copy of the relation set beside the vocabulary-driven declare_object_properties list (turtle.rs:678-691); a relation the vocabulary adds is declared but never stubbed." WebVOWL iterates a hardcoded REL_MAP and "the two agree only while the vocabulary does" (webvowl.rs:30-42 vs turtle.rs:656-673). Four hand-kept orderings exist: RELATION_KEYS (ir/model.rs:36), SCAFFOLD_REL_ORDER (indexes.rs:30), PAGE_API_REL_ORDER (page_api.rs:18), REL_MAP (webvowl.rs:30).
failure: the vocabulary gains a thirteenth relation: Turtle declares the property but emits no stub concept for undeclared targets (dangling references), WebVOWL silently drops every such edge, and the ordering tables omit it from the scaffold and page API. Published artefacts disagree with each other and with the vocabulary, with no refusal anywhere.

title: Generation identity is not what it claims: the digest excludes the profile and roster, caller-supplied commit/dirty are taken verbatim, and two different roots stand in for one directory
evidence: "the attribution roster shapes the Turtle and the page API but is not an input to content_digest (mod.rs:688-693 vs 971-991)"; reproduced in OM-11.3: a page-namespace change "preserved generation ID and content digest while changing page IRIs and artefact hashes," and "caller-provided commit and dirty flag are accepted directly (mod.rs:925,926)" — an arbitrary commit label was retained. The vocabulary directory is hard-coded to `repo_root/ontology` for dirtiness while the roster is read from `vault_root.parent()/ontology` (mod.rs:941, attribution.rs:32); for a flat layout the roster is looked up one directory above the repository (OM-03.2 Debt).
failure: a consumer cache keyed on `content_digest` (C3 itself notes Loom consumers must key on scope too) serves stale pages after a profile change; a generation stamp asserts a commit the build never verified; flat-layout vaults publish without attribution and mis-report dirty, silently.
marked_by_authors: yes (TENSION/DIVERGENCE OM-11.3; DIVERGENCE N1/N3 and Debt in OM-03.6/OM-03.2)

title: In the Obsidian host, an index failure rejects after the write has persisted, two query blocks in one note defeat the request guard, and a timeout cannot recall the request
evidence: "rejection can follow persisted write; upsert is outside write-error catch (api.ts:248,253)" — reproduced. The query channel is the note path, so "two blocks in one note collide (sparql-block.ts:71)" and the latest-request-wins guard (guard.ts:46,68) cancels one block's result against the other's. "Timeout races host request; no abort handle (ingest-transport.ts:85,91,92)" — it stops waiting, it does not recall. There is also "no second abort check after optional Jev judging and before confirmation."
failure: the user confirms an ingest edit; the write lands; the index update throws; the plugin reports failure. The user retries (duplicate application) or discards an edit that actually persisted — vault state and the user's belief diverge. In one note, a saved query shows another block's stale-or-cancelled result.

title: The amend write path compares and renames with no writer lock, and the git push can carry commits that landed after the ahead-count check
evidence: "compare and rename are separate; no writer lock at this boundary (write/apply.rs:401,411)" — marked OPEN; the audit says "the file re-read/rename interval remains a source-level concern." Also "writer can add a commit after count; push then includes it (ontology-apply.js:872,879)."
failure: a governance apply re-reads the target, a user edit lands in the interval, and the rename clobbers the user's change silently — the applied proposal is valid, the lost edit is unrecorded. Or the publication push carries an unrelated commit that arrived between the count and the push, attaching it to the governance change.
confidence: medium (asserted at source level; the audit did not reproduce the interleaving)
marked_by_authors: yes (OPEN for the race; TENSION for the push)

title: A missing working vault is silently skipped on the publication load, so `build --vault all` can publish an incomplete bundle that only one CI workflow catches
evidence: `sibling_vault(Working)` is "loaded with the layout's excluded dirs only if that directory exists (build/publish.rs:365-376)" and feeds `publish_vaults` (mod.rs:612-618); the MissingVault refusal covers only the primary root (`root_of` refusals, main.rs:457-466, profile.rs:573-588), and layout validation "retains missing optional leaves" (OM-12.1). The authors state the consequence without flagging it as a defect: visionGraph checks that both trees exist "because ontomark silently accepts a knowledge-only build (publish.yml:199-205)."
failure: a checkout or mount where `working/` is absent or misnamed produces a successful `--vault all` build whose `publish/` tree lacks the working pages entirely. visionGraph's workflow compensates; any other consumer, or a local build, ships the incomplete publication with exit 0.
confidence: high on the behaviour (author-stated); the mechanism (conditional sibling load bypassing the primary-root refusal) is inferred from the cited lines
marked_by_authors: no — the compensating CI check is recorded as an invariant; the gap itself carries no Tension/Debt/Drift/Open marker

title: The still-running VisionClaw publish job ships the fail-open redactor and the body-only credential scan
evidence: OM-00.3 EXT: "VisionClaw's vault build job still ships S1.1, S1.2, S1.5, S2.3 and S3.1 unchanged until VC-60 retires under its four gates" (ADR-OM-005-estate-alignment:28). S1.2 origin: body-only scan, frontmatter published (vault/src/build/publish.rs:159-160, :196; d5c1188 wrapped link redaction round render, not the scan). S1.1 origin: fail-open redactor (vault/src/projection.rs:230). Both were fixed only in ontomark 8d654d1 (OM-00.2 A1, A2), a different binary. OM-05.5 n2: the retirement is gated "so it keeps running".
failure: ADR-OM-005 retires the legacy `vault` producer but the retirement is gated, so VisionClaw's `ontology-publish.yml` keeps running. It builds the in-tree legacy crate (`cargo build -p vault`, ontology-publish.yml:167-168) and runs `vault build --vault knowledge` (ontology-publish.yml:172-175). That crate still carries S1.1 and S1.2 unfixed: the credential scan reads the page body only while render re-emits the frontmatter into `publish/`, and the prose redactor fails open on a regex compile error. A credential-shaped string in a public page's frontmatter value (sources, title) is never scanned, is re-emitted by render, and ships in the pod-resource pack (ontology-publish.yml:247). Independently, any redactor compile failure in that job silently disables private-link redaction.
confidence: high that these faults ship in the live job; the triggering content is inferred (routine authoring).

title: A private working note's name survives in a public knowledge title
evidence: OM-11.2 GAP: "bare private working name can survive in a public knowledge title; knowledge redactor is not the union redactor" (projection.rs:750, :850, :890); reproduced: "The same private working-note title was masked in a public working title and retained in a public knowledge title. Both public and machine builds retained the latter." Knowledge side built first from its own records (projection.rs:750-751); union markers built over the union set (projection.rs:837-850) and applied only to working records (projection.rs:869-875); page title taken from the projected record (page_api.rs:89).
failure: Under machine scope (and the equivalent public working publish), the knowledge projection is built first through its own record set and is deliberately untouched by working (D4), so the marker set used to mask knowledge prose is the knowledge-only set, not the union set built later. A public knowledge page whose title/label names a private working note passes through unmasked; the union redactor is applied only to surviving working records. The unmasked title is emitted into the page API, search index, scaffold and Turtle. A client reading the public artefacts sees the private note's name.

title: A governance decision can be applied to one page while the receipt and ledger attest another
evidence: OM-07.1 X (TENSION, :444 vs :400); OM-07.2 GAP (DRIFT, ontology-apply.js:570 vs write/create.rs:258), including the reproduced A/B fixture; OM-07.3 LEDGER and RACE/OTHER markers; the topic's business statement: "The application can make a valid local change while its receipt names a different page or case."
failure: Approve checks that the proposal digest equals the decision tag (local-process-manager.js:400); the explicit promote path checks only the request tag and signed IRI and lacks that equality check (local-process-manager.js:444). The adapter reconstructs staged Markdown from the proposal's added diff lines (ontology-apply.js:560, :578); `ontomark create` derives the target filename from the parsed title of that staged file (write/create.rs:248, :258), which can differ from the proposal page slug checked earlier (ontology-apply.js:570). Page B is created exclusively; the adapter receipt names the original proposal page A (ontology-apply.js:634) and the ledger attests the caller's case and digest after the write (ontology-apply.js:742, :900). The corpus now contains B while the audit trail says A under case C. The push-after-commit-count window can additionally carry another writer's commit (ontology-apply.js:872, :879), and the apply compare/rename pair has no writer lock (write/apply.rs:401, :411).
confidence: high for the identity disagreement (reproduced); the signed forum-to-corpus journey is not certified by the audit (inferred).

title: `publish_out` is written after promote, so the live site and the bundle stop being one generation
evidence: "write_to runs AFTER promote, so a failure there leaves the NEW bundle beside the PREVIOUS publication tree that swap_in kept, the two no longer one generation" (build/publish.rs:356, build/mod.rs:1026-1028). visionGraph passes `--publish-out quartz/content` (publish.yml:175-181).
failure: a build that withdraws or redacts a page promotes the bundle and markers, `write_to` then fails, and the public site keeps serving the withdrawn content while the marker claims the new generation.

title: The compat projection publishes held-back `misc/` pages into every data artefact while `publish/` skips them
evidence: "the compat path never forces misc/ pages private (held_back is only applied in the link path ir/projection.rs:616); a public misc/ page stays public there, while stage_redacted skips it build/publish.rs:220" (OM-02.3 n1; OM-00.1 H4, KEEP S3.4).
failure: any build run with `--no-redact-private-links` emits site-only `misc/` content into ontology.ttl, indexes, page API, search, tiers and OKF; a reviewer checking only `publish/` believes it withheld.
confidence: high (stated; requires the opt-out flag, default off)

title: The held-page identity rule is narrower than the staging rule, and migrate compiles without the redactor
evidence: `is_unpublished` covers `_misc` at top level only (input/page.rs:48, :667) while `held_back` applies `_misc` at any depth plus `misc` (build/publish.rs:134, :138-148); "the census and excluded_identities_of still use the top-level-only is_unpublished (projection.rs:114, :231), which is the divergence that remains" (OM-03.3). Migrate keeps its own excluded-identity loop on the narrow rule (migrate/compile.rs:38-39, :105-114) and compiles through `project`, "the thin wrapper dropping the redactor" (ir/projection.rs:440-446; caller migrate/compile.rs:116).
failure: on the compat and migrate paths, a held page outside the narrow rule is neither forced private nor identity-masked, and `api/census.json` counts disagree with what staging withheld.
confidence: high for the rule divergence; medium (inferred) for what migrate's output exposes
marked_by_authors: yes (DIVERGENCE; the redactor-less migrate path is stated but unmarked)

title: Certificate evidence can be absent, stale, or deleted relative to the published bundle
evidence: `certificate_out` defaults to absent and then "nothing written, nothing checked" (build/mod.rs:738, main.rs:410) although ADR-OM-009 is titled "every published closure carries a derivation certificate" (Open in OM-03.8). Certificate files are written directly before the consistency gate with no bundle transaction (build/mod.rs:723-725); an unsatisfiable refusal leaves "the old bundle can retain new certificate beside it" (mod.rs:744, OM-10.2); a certificate inside the output directory "is removed by successful replacement" (mod.rs:311, :313, :316). C3 lists no certificate output (sovereign-corpus-contracts.md:111 vs ADR-OM-009:34).
failure: a shipped generation carries no warrant, or a warrant describing a graph that was never published; a client re-verifying with oo-cert either finds nothing or proves the wrong closure.

title: An ingest rerun replaces a complete review bundle; evidence is not retained
evidence: the request ID omits the endpoint though cache and parser include it (ingest_cmd.rs:606 vs :570, :446); the manifest directory is removed before rewrite (ingest_cmd.rs:771-772); "incomplete uncached rerun can replace complete bundle under same ID" (ingest_cmd.rs:723, :769, :772); source snapshots, prior target bytes and model requests are not retained (ingest_cmd.rs:802-838). Removed-source classification exists in the library (ledger.rs:224, :255) but the host records only finished observed sources (ingest_cmd.rs:841, :843).
failure: a reviewer's accepted evidence is silently destroyed by a later failed rerun and cannot be replayed or audited; withdrawn sources vanish from reports.

title: The mention check accepts a negated relation
evidence: "Quote must mention the value accept.rs:533"; TENSION: "mention check does not prove relation meaning; a negated relation can pass" — a reproduced negative sentence grounds an accepted positive relation.
failure: an applied assertion contradicts its own cited source; the corpus gains a false relation whose evidence quote looks supportive to a reviewer.

title: The reasoner extractor drops unknown shapes and unreadable definitions before the refusal check
evidence: "unknown shapes and unreadable definitions can be omitted before refusal check" (ontomark-compile/src/reason.rs:283, :401); "A malformed graph definition was also omitted"; a raw universal restriction produced zero compiler refusals while the typed equivalent was refused. Repeated as AUDIT LIMIT in OM-04.3; `reason.rs` unchanged between that audit and 4b9d15d.
failure: a malformed definition on a page is silently ignored; an incomplete closure is published with no refusal, and consumers cannot distinguish it from a complete one.
confidence: high (probes reproduced); production reach via authored pages is inferred

title: Obsidian persists the write, then the index update can fail, leaving the engine on stale text
evidence: atomic full-text comparison and write (api.ts:242-246), then index update (api.ts:253); TENSION: "rejection can follow persisted write; upsert is outside write-error catch" (api.ts:248, :253); OM-06.5 Open: "a later index failure can reject after persistence"; the engine's caches rebuild only on upsert g+1 (engine.rs:304-314).
failure: the confirmed edit is on disk but the engine still holds the old text; a later ingest preview/apply built on the stale base can overwrite the user's persisted edit — silent loss of a confirmed change.
confidence: high for the divergence; the overwrite chain is inferred

title: No abort re-check between judging and confirmation; a timeout cannot recall the request
evidence: abort is checked only between chunks (ingest-transport.ts:149, :152); "Timeout races host request; no abort handle" (ingest-transport.ts:85, :91-92); "The current host has no second abort check after optional Jev judging and before confirmation."
failure: a request the user cancelled or that timed out still produces a preview that can be confirmed and applied.

title: NGG1 silently drops edges to non-selected targets and collapses all relation identity
evidence: "Edge to a target that is not a selected node is silently dropped" (graph_tiers.rs:297-298, :309-310); twelve relation keys become one `EDGE_RELATION` byte and the dedup key merges distinct relations between one pair (graph_tiers.rs:283, :313-315); `EDGE_RELATION` is a published wire value (ontomark-ngg1/src/lib.rs:142-144); only `stats.json` reports declared against shipped.
failure: an agent consuming the tiers answers from a graph missing relations, with no refusal, and cannot distinguish part-of from related-to.
confidence: high (stated, OPEN S3.1); consumer consequence inferred

title: The certificate checker passes an empty derivation file; the writer is not atomic
evidence: "omitting all steps still passes; soundness does not establish closure completeness" (oo_cert.rs:55-56, reproduced truncation); "failed second write can leave new assertions with old digest" (rdfs-certificate/src/lib.rs:589-590); scope.tsv and asserted.sha256 are not inputs to the checker invocation (oo_cert.rs:54-56).
failure: a truncated or partially-written certificate passes independent re-verification, so a client's check "succeeds" against evidence that proves nothing about the shipped closure.

title: The profile is absent from `content_digest`, and caller-supplied commit/dirty are trusted
evidence: "profile is absent from content_digest inputs; same digest can accompany changed output" (mod.rs:963-983), reproduced with a namespace change altering page IRIs; "Caller-provided commit and dirty flag are accepted directly" (mod.rs:925-926).
failure: a consumer cache keyed on content_digest serves artefacts built under the old profile; a caller-supplied commit label misattributes provenance in the marker.

title: The attribution roster is read from a different root than the ontology, and is not in the digest
evidence: the roster is read from `vault_root.parent()` (build/mod.rs:688-692, attribution.rs:32) while dirtiness reads `repo_root/ontology` (mod.rs:941); a flat layout roots the vault at `repo_root` (profile.rs:520-524, :561-562), so the roster is looked up above the repository; the roster is not an input to `content_digest` (mod.rs:971-991).
failure: a flat vault publishes Turtle and page API with an empty roster (absent file is an empty roster, attribution.rs:29-37) and attribution edits never change the digest.
confidence: medium (path divergence and empty-roster behaviour stated; the flat-vault consequence inferred)

title: `retrieve`, `tree` and `edit` silently take only the first vault under `--vault all`
evidence: "retrieve, tree and edit call .next() on the loaded vaults, so under all they read knowledge alone" (main.rs:936-939, :961-964, :984-987), against the stated rule that `all` means both.
failure: an operator editing under `--vault all` touches the knowledge page only; a same-id working page is silently unchanged and later merges behave unexpectedly.

title: A missing working directory makes `--vault all` silently publish knowledge only
evidence: the sibling working vault is loaded "only if that directory exists" (build/mod.rs:612-613, build/publish.rs:365-376); "ontomark silently accepts a knowledge-only build" and only visionGraph's workflow guards it by requiring both trees (publish.yml:199-205).
failure: a renamed or missing working root publishes an incomplete corpus with no warning; consumers outside that one workflow (e.g. machine bundles) ship incomplete data.
confidence: high for the mechanism; the consumer consequence inferred
marked_by_authors: no (stated; the workflow guard is labelled invariant)

title: The MRC20 deposit path credits self-asserted amounts on a one-string proof
evidence: `verify_mrc20_anchor` walks only the caller-supplied `stateStrings`; only the last is compared with `JCS(state)` (mrc20.rs:1061), "nothing requires … one string per state since genesis", and mark 0's input is never examined (blocktrail.rs:1114), so "with one string there is no earlier mark to walk". The head address "is derived from the public issuer key alone … funding it needs no issuer secret" (mrc20.rs:766). On deposit, the credited amount is whatever `state.ops` transfers (mrc20.rs:253), bounded only by a 21-million per-credit ceiling (payments.rs:469, :622); "Nothing on this path rejects such a proof" (handlers/pay.rs:603-620); the anchor network comes from the body, defaulting to testnet4 (handlers/pay.rs:566); the replay guard is per outpoint; and a head still in the mempool passes as intact. The whole `/pay/*` surface is mounted with no feature flag (lib.rs:5282) while the README claims payments are added "through explicit features" (README.md:3).
failure: an attacker derives the issuer's head address from the public key, funds one UTXO themselves, posts a one-string MRC20 deposit asserting an arbitrary transfer to their own pod account, and is credited token units they can then trade or withdraw; repeatable with fresh outpoints, each credit self-asserted up to the ceiling.
confidence: high (the code path is stated consistently across three panels; the authors note it is source tracing only, no request was sent)
marked_by_authors: yes (Tension at SP-07.9 and SP-07.17; DIVERGENCE at SP-07.14)

title: The provenance commit query leaks private resources' metadata and sidecar text unauthenticated
evidence: the `_prov` GET path has "no resource WAC gate or sidecar commit check; anchored is a substring check for bt:txid" (handlers/prov.rs:413), and the observed behaviour is that "private resource and sidecar reads returned 401 in the audit fixture, while the unauthenticated commit query returned their metadata and sidecar text". The route family registers before the LDP catch-all (handlers/prov.rs:747). The write side compounds it: an accepted anchor "replace[s] current sidecar even for old commit; write failure logged, still 200 and charged" (handlers/prov.rs:584).
failure: an unauthenticated caller queries commit metadata for private resources and reads their provenance sidecars, disclosing the existence, authorship and anchoring of data the ACL hides; an owner operation can also silently leave a sidecar describing the wrong commit.

title: The production consumer is pinned to a revision that predates four security repairs, with the mirror compiled in
evidence: agentbox pins `0.5.0-alpha.18` at rev `76ab7aab` (agentbox/lib/solid-pod-rs.nix:54-58), which "predates its crate fixes: SP-GIT-02 commits A, B1 and B2, the hidden-object fetch refusal, the NIP-98 empty-body binding, the OIDC redirect check and the ACL-control fix" — those fixes live only at `8f2df86`, `fcc624a`, `daff10d` and the topic head, under `[Unreleased]` (CHANGELOG.md:7), so the version string does not reveal the gap. The same flake compiles `forge-full` unless `forge.enable` is false (agentbox/flake.nix:1548): "A shipped agentbox build therefore carries the pre-repair mirror; it stays inert only while no follow entries are configured."
failure: every incident class already fixed at head is live in the deployed binary: NIP-98 events minted over content reusable to blank the resource (across the restart/replica replay gaps), JWKS fetching that follows redirects, the syntactic lockout guard that accepted wrong-target Control, and a mirror whose held objects can be fetched by SHA once any follow entry exists.
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt at SP-09.7; Tension at SP-08.18)

title: Lenient Turtle ACL parsing drops conditions, turning restricted grants into unconditional ones
evidence: "a lenient Turtle parse can report Found after discarding a condition" (SP-04.3 Debt); the parser stops on unbalanced brackets (wac/parser.rs:317-320) and returns None on an absent condition type (parser.rs:418), yet `parse_turtle_acl` "Ok, including partially parsed rules" maps to Found (resolver.rs:295 in SP-04.4). Evaluation gates conjunctively over only the retained conditions (evaluator.rs:309), and the audience re-evaluation "use[s] the parsed document, including any restrictions already lost by the parser", so "lost restrictions can misclassify a response as Public" (SP-03.12 Boundary).
failure: a Turtle ACL whose payment, client or origin condition has a syntax defect — one unbalanced bracket suffices — is enforced as an unconditional grant of the modes and agents it names, and affected reads are classified Public and cached accordingly.
marked_by_authors: yes (Debt at SP-04.3 and SP-04.10; Boundary at SP-03.12)

title: Inner-container `.acl` files are write-protected but never enforced, and migration leaves them dead
evidence: `protected_resource_for_acl` maps `/dir/.acl` to `/dir/` (wac/mod.rs:220) so writing it needs Control on `/dir/`, but the resolver reads `acl_sidecar_key("/dir/")` = `/dir.acl` (resolver.rs:333-338, :379) — "a stored `/dir/.acl` is protected but never enforced". Discovery now advertises `/dir.acl` (ldp.rs:152) and "the upstream changelog leaves existing inner copies to a migration review rather than moving them"; SP-13.2 confirms the mapping "does not relocate old inner policies or choose between conflicting files".
failure: on upgrade, every pre-existing inner-container ACL silently stops governing its container; access falls back to whatever the ancestor chain grants — typically more permissive than the dead file. If the owner's only Control grant lived in the dead file, they are additionally locked out of writing the corrected `/dir.acl`.

title: Self-service provisioning writes no ACL: fresh pods are either locked out or governed by unreviewed inheritance
evidence: "provision_named_pod writes no `.acl`. A pod created through `/.pods` or `/api/accounts/new` is governed by whatever ACL its ancestors carry. This review did not trace what the root ACL grants a fresh pod" (SP-06.8 Open). The resolver denies by default: Missing → "deny by default (no ACL means no access)" (SP-04.3). Only the admin route writes an owner-only ACL (lib.rs:4527-4533).
failure: a user creates a pod, receives 201 with webId and podUri, and then — if no ancestor grants — cannot write anything, including the `.acl` (sidecar writes need Control): total self-lockout. If an ancestor carries a broad `acl:default` grant, every fresh pod's content is readable by that grant from birth. Both branches are untested.
confidence: high that no ACL is written; medium (inferred) on which branch manifests, since the root ACL was not traced

title: A transient storage read error can replace the canonical payment state with stale mirrors, losing intents
evidence: `read_state_unchecked` — "any get error falls back to legacy files, version zero and no pending intents" (handlers/pay.rs:184); "a read outage can select stale mirrors and the next successful write can replace the canonical state with them, losing intents and resetting the version". Recovery "trusts explorer presence, advances a saved trail when behind and reverses a payout on 404. A missing payout receipt retains the intent" (pay.rs:242).
failure: a brief storage read failure during a payout window causes the next successful write to overwrite the authoritative ledger/replay/market bundle with stale mirror files — pending broadcast intents vanish (double-payout exposure) and the version counter resets; in the opposite direction a missing receipt keeps an intent that may re-pay.

title: Git export selects the wrong repository and gates whole-history export on pod-root Read only
evidence: the pod component is applied twice — a request to `/alice/info/refs` sets the adapter root to `data_root/alice` (lib.rs:4740), then the service "extract slug and join to root again" and looks for the repository at `data_root/alice/alice` (service.rs:295, :299, :338); "The normal write hook records files under `data_root/alice`, so this is a different repository selection." Independently, clone and fetch "check Read only on the pod-root resource" (lib.rs:4792, :4797) with "no child ACL walk here" before the CGI (service.rs:378), while `git_mark_write` commits private content into that history (mark.rs:168).
failure: with the git feature compiled (forge-full implies it), a clone either 404s — the advertised export is broken — or, where a nested repository happens to exist at `data_root/<pod>/<pod>`, serves that repository's contents to anyone holding Read on the pod root; and once selection is corrected, the intended pod history would export every private child's current and historical content under the same root-only grant.
confidence: high on the selection and gate facts (stated with lines); the wrong-repo-serving branch requires a nested repository to exist (inferred)
severity: medium (becomes high the moment repository selection is fixed without an export-authority contract)
marked_by_authors: yes (Boundary at SP-14.2 and SP-06.12); the SP-14.1 double-join itself carries no marker

title: All serialisation is process-local: money, quota, provenance and replay state corrupt with two replicas or across restarts
evidence: "PAYMENT_STATE_LOCK is process-wide, not storage-wide — two replicas over one pod store share no lock" (lib.rs:208); "trail and epoch locks are in-process and held across network calls" (W8); the replay store: "Restart forgets ids, replicas do not share state" (replay_store.rs:115); the FsBackend lock "is process-local. A second process writing the same root is not serialised … between the two renames it can read a stale sidecar's content type" (SP-06.4); quota reserve reads `head()` before taking the per-pod lock, so concurrent overwrites of one resource drift the counter until reconcile (lib.rs:2661-2667).
failure: horizontally scaling the server over one data root — the obvious production posture — yields lost updates on balances and orders, double-crediting, torn metadata/content-type pairs and quota drift; even single-instance, each restart reopens the NIP-98 replay window for one TTL, and a hung explorer call stalls writers holding the trail lock.
confidence: high (stated repeatedly; the two-replica scenario is the direct implication)
marked_by_authors: yes (W3/W4/W8 notes, LIMIT at SP-05.5, invariant note at SP-06.4, Open at SP-06.6 and SP-07.7)

title: Replay protections degrade: the DPoP cache evicts unexpired entries, and the NIP-98 TTL is unvalidated
evidence: the DPoP jti cache's "capacity insertion evicts LRU, even unexpired" (oidc/replay.rs:177) — unlike the NIP-98 store which refuses at capacity (replay_store.rs:75); the NIP-98 "TTL is not validated against token freshness. Environment accepts any positive seconds. Constructor also permits zero" (replay.rs:133, :149) while the freshness window is ±60 s (nip98.rs:28), a two-sided 120 s window; restart forgets ids (replay_store.rs:115).
failure: under jti pressure a captured DPoP proof becomes replayable once its still-unexpired entry is evicted; an operator who sets a replay TTL below 120 s (or zero) silently reopens NIP-98 replay for every credential; every restart reopens the same window.
marked_by_authors: partly — the NIP-98 process-local and TTL facts are marked (LIMIT notes, SP-05.4/SP-05.5); the DPoP LRU eviction at SP-05.7 carries no marker

title: The server challenges with DPoP and Bearer but can verify neither on resources; production Bearer is silently anonymous
evidence: every ACL denial returns "WWW-Authenticate: Nostr, DPoP, Bearer — all three realms" (lib.rs:1136); yet in a production build "every Bearer header is anonymous" (lib.rs:617) and the extractor has "no DPoP dispatch" (lib.rs:635) — SP-12.2: "resource extractor handles Nostr; production Bearer refused, no DPoP dispatch … challenge nevertheless advertises DPoP" (lib.rs:1140, :1160). The crate ships an OIDC IdP and an `oidc_client` example, and the material states OIDC components "do not yet provide an external-client private-resource journey on the main pod server".
failure: a standards-conforming Solid-OIDC client completes the flow against the bundled IdP, receives a valid DPoP-bound token, follows the server's own challenge, and is refused 401 indefinitely — private resources are unreachable for the entire OIDC ecosystem the crate advertises; Bearer integrations fail closed while looking like a client credential problem.
confidence: high (each fact stated; the contradiction is direct)
marked_by_authors: no — each half is stated, but no marker joins the advertised challenge to the verifier gap

title: POST unique-name minting is check-then-act: concurrent Slugs silently overwrite
evidence: "mint_unique_target probes with exists and the later put is a plain write (lib.rs:1771, :1865), so the no-overwrite rule is a check-then-act. Two concurrent POSTs with the same Slug can both choose the same free name. The hash fallback is a deterministic hash of the target, so it is not guaranteed fresh either (lib.rs:1788)."
failure: two clients POST the same Slug concurrently; both receive 201 with a Location naming the same resource and the second `put` silently replaces the first body — created data lost with no error to either client.
confidence: medium — the authors state the source permits it but that "only a concurrent run could confirm the race"

title: JSON Patch applied to a non-JSON body destroys the stored content where the RDF dialects would refuse
evidence: "The JSON Patch branch treats a stored body that is not JSON as `{}` and writes the patched object back under the stored content type (lib.rs:1949-1952, :1978). So a JSON Patch that applies cleanly to an empty object, sent to a Turtle resource, replaces its triples where an N3 patch would be refused."
failure: a client (or middleware that auto-selects the patch dialect) sends `application/json-patch` to an RDF resource; the server applies it to an empty object and stores the result, silently replacing the resource's entire triple content without the 409 the RDF paths give.

title: The shipped `account delete` command can never delete anything but reports "no such user"
evidence: "the shipped account delete builds a fresh InMemoryUserStore inside dispatch (cli/mod.rs:380), so it can never find a real user and always reports 'no such user'. Its help text promises removal of pods and the WebID profile as well (cli/mod.rs:105), but nothing on that path touches either."

title: MRC20 deposit credited on a one-string trail proof: self-asserted balances drained real value

SP-07.9 N5: only the last string is compared with `JCS(state)` (`solid-pod-rs/src/mrc20.rs:1061`); "nothing requires JCS(prevState) or a seq-0 genesis among them". SP-07.17 Tension: the credited amount "is whatever `state.ops` transfer to the pod's address (`solid-pod-rs/src/mrc20.rs:253`), and no balance or supply rule limits it beyond the 21-million-coin ceiling (`solid-pod-rs/src/payments.rs:469`, `:622`)"; "Nothing on this path rejects such a proof (`solid-pod-rs-server/src/handlers/pay.rs:603-620`)"; the anchor network comes from the body, defaulting to testnet4 (`solid-pod-rs-server/src/handlers/pay.rs:566`); "The server's route tests have no one-string or head-only negative case." SP-07.19 confirms mark 0's input is never examined on the walk (`solid-pod-rs/src/blocktrail.rs:1114`).

They craft a state JSON whose `ops` transfer a large amount of the configured ticker to their own pod address and submit `POST /pay/.deposit` with a valid NIP-98 header, supplying a one-element `stateStrings` proof. `verify_mrc20_anchor` walks "every earlier mark", but with one string there is no earlier mark, so mark 0's input is never examined and the check collapses to the head-only form. The outpoint replay guard passes (each attack uses a fresh outpoint), and `credit_by_outpoint` credits the attacker's ticker balance with the self-asserted amount. The attacker swaps the credited tokens through the always-mounted AMM/order book, or withdraws them — the counterparty pools holding real user value absorb the loss.
confidence: high — the code path and the absent rejection are stated at the cited lines; the material recorded "source tracing at 9b6143c only: no request was sent", so end-to-end exploitation was never reproduced in the record.

SP-06.11: every LDP write is marked (`Marked --> Marked: git-mark per PUT / POST / PATCH`); SP-07.1 D: DELETE bypasses marking, so history retains prior versions of deleted files. SP-10.8 N2 / CHANGELOG.md:557: alpha.13 guidance addresses "an operator who served a public-read root", establishing that public-root deployments exist. confidence: high — the root-only gate, the absence of per-child/historical WAC, and the double-join are all stated; that the join was corrected in the intervening twelve months (the precondition for exposure) is inferred.

title: Lenient Turtle ACL parsing silently dropped a restriction; the truncated rule granted unconditionally and the response was classified Public
evidence: SP-04.3 Debt: "a lenient Turtle parse can report Found after discarding a condition", with native probes referenced. SP-04.10: "unbalanced brackets stop parsing (`solid-pod-rs/src/wac/parser.rs:317-320`)"; "absent type returns None (`solid-pod-rs/src/wac/parser.rs:418`)". SP-03.3 Note: "DEBT valid Turtle with incomplete condition shape can pass (`solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs:1668`)". SP-04.7: the condition gate is conjunctive over the retained conditions (`solid-pod-rs/src/wac/evaluator.rs:309`); a rule with no retained conditions has none to fail. SP-03.12 Boundary: "Lost restrictions can misclassify a response as Public. Headers do not prove revocation through an intermediary cache." SP-04.6 Debt: "the guard still evaluates what the lenient Turtle reader retained, so a condition the parser discards is invisible to it as it is to enforcement."
failure: An operator writes an ACL in Turtle intended to restrict a rule (for example a Read grant gated by a condition). The condition block has a shape the parser mishandles — unbalanced brackets stop parsing at that point, or a condition with an absent type returns None — and the condition is discarded while the authorization, with its agent and mode triples, still lands in the document as `Found`. The PUT path accepts the file, because "valid Turtle with incomplete condition shape can pass" validation. At evaluation the rule now has an empty condition list; the conjunctive gate requires all conditions to be Satisfied and trivially passes, so the mode is granted to whoever the agent clause names — including `foaf:Agent`. The anonymous re-evaluation for audience runs over the same truncated document, grants, and the response is classified Public. Private data becomes world-readable, with cache treatment for a Public audience; nothing logs a policy problem, because both enforcement and the lockout guard evaluate only what the parser retained.
confidence: high — the parser loss, its acceptance at write time, and the empty-condition grant are each stated; the specific operator-authored Turtle shape that triggers it in production is inferred.

title: NIP-98 tokens on `/solid` never bind the write body
evidence: `extract_user_identity` calls `validate_nip98_token(token, &expected_url, expected_method, None)` (`src/handlers/solid_proxy_handler.rs:225`); with `BodyBinding::RequiredWhenTagged` (`src/utils/nip98.rs:439`) and no body, the catch-all `(RequiredWhenTagged, _, _) => {}` (`nip98.rs:556`) matches, so a `payload` tag is never compared on `/solid` PUT/POST/PATCH; the `/solid` scope adds no other body check (`solid_proxy_handler.rs:1773-1807`). Token lifetime 60 s (`nip98.rs:169`); single-use claim (`nip98.rs:573`) limits the attack to one substitution per token. The material parallels SP-ID-01 in `docs/estate-review/2026-11-01-solid-identity-boundaries.md`.
failure: an attacker who captures an unused signed token (log leak, proxy, client compromise) substitutes different bytes to the same URL+method inside the 60 s window — e.g. replaces an agent-memory JSON-LD document or a graph view the victim was about to write.

title: ElevationActor loses approved, PR-tracked cases on restart

title: First-contact decisions are ungated and `approvedBy` is unverified: attributed summary writebacks can be fabricated

title: An explicit `public: false` is overridden by any valid `owl-class` marker

title: Nonce replay protection is a 4096-entry LRU shared across all sessions

The material does not state eviction→replay explicitly; that step is inferred from the bounded LRU.

marked_by_authors: no (recency-over-completeness is stated as design, not flagged).

title: The amendment apply path persists a page whose resource IRI differs from the approved one; there is no after-application identity check

DRIFT: fixture page now has replacement resource; no after-resource equality check (write/apply.rs:280,282)". "A real signed producer output changes the resource through the real CLI writer. The old-resource equality check passes because the page still has its original identity before application." title: Governed push-to-talk never dispatches the speaker's own utterance and fires signed governed commands on status strings and other users' transcripts

Each of those is sent as a governed voice_command for the bound DID." VC-35.6 DEBT confirms status strings share the transcript channel (speech_service.rs:429, :464).

confidence: high on the mechanism (material states it, "Source tracing only, not exercised"); the frequency of spurious dispatches in real rooms is inferred.

title: The consumer cannot apply the producer's signed grouped proposals: the identity check fails before the writer is ever invoked
evidence: The producer signs groups ("Group subject is proposal IRI", vault-core/src/proposal.rs:225, :234; "Any new page makes group kind create", propose.rs:590; "Postable group can be signed", main.rs:500, :516). title: The proposal case digest is stable while the assessed consequences are not, and versionIRI-only differences produce non-conservative verdicts

Also VC-41.1: "Consequences do not automatically raise the level."

Separately, every rebuild that only bumps versionIRI reports added-and-lost triples, so non-conservative verdicts fire on logically identical content and train reviewers to dismiss the signal. Neither EL equivalence nor review-context identity is established by either mechanism.
confidence: high on the mechanism (both stated); medium on the operational effect (inferred)

title: Failed settings writes are silently deleted from the retry queue and the auth-failure signal has no listener

title: The speech socket admits anonymous peers into an ungoverned server-side command path and into every other user's transcripts
evidence: "started() subscribes this socket to the SpeechService audio and transcription broadcasts before any authenticate frame (speech_socket_handler.rs:511-541), and the forwarders write to the socket with no pubkey check (:556-558, :571-583). For up to AUTH_DEADLINE an unauthenticated peer receives every TTS chunk and transcript broadcast to all sockets. ADR-2075 guards inbound commands only" (VC-35.4); "Binary audio frames are NOT behind the gate: the Binary arm :956-976 forwards any frame to process_audio_chunk without a pubkey check"; "authenticate is the ONLY frame accepted while pubkey is None … reject_unauthenticated (speech_socket_handler.rs:133, applied :627-633) refuses tts, stt, voice_command, set_ptt and cancel_tts" — i.e. the gate covers exactly the frames an attacker does not need. "a Whisper transcript that contains any of 20 keywords (agent, node, graph, run, show…) is ALSO executed server-side: is_voice_command, VoiceCommand::parse and execute_voice_command_with_context (src/services/speech_service.rs:620-633, :1032-1060, :1062), which can call swarm init and agent spawn on MCP_HOST (:1066-1068, :1079, :1086). That path has no actorDid, no clarification gate and no signature" (VC-35.6); "both actors consume the GLOBAL transcript broadcast, so speech from any connected speech socket - including one not yet authenticated (VC-35.4) - can open a settings-assistant task or an elevation case. Neither path carries a speaker identity" (VC-35.10); "The broadcast is global, so every connected speech socket plays every utterance" (VC-35.9); `AUTH_DEADLINE` = 30 s, speech_socket_handler.rs:22, :487-500.
failure: A peer on the network opens `/ws/speech`. ADR-2075 checks no credential at upgrade — "the socket opens anonymous and useless" for JSON commands only. On `started()` the socket is subscribed to the SpeechService audio and transcription broadcasts *before* any authenticate frame, and the forwarders write with no pubkey check, so for up to `AUTH_DEADLINE` (30 s) — and repeatedly, by reconnecting — the anonymous peer receives every TTS chunk and every transcript broadcast to all sockets. Independently, binary frames bypass the auth gate entirely: the Binary arm forwards any frame to `process_audio_chunk` without a pubkey check. The attacker sends audio; Whisper transcribes it; `is_voice_command` / `VoiceCommand::parse` / `execute_voice_command_with_context` executes it server-side — swarm init and agent spawn on `MCP_HOST` — with no actorDid, no clarification gate and no signature. In parallel, any transcript on the global broadcast reaches `VoiceInterfaceActor` and `ElevationActor` with no speaker identity, so an unauthenticated socket's speech can open a settings-assistant task or a persisted elevation case. Authenticated victims' TTS audio is itself broadcast to every connected socket.
confidence: high — every gate omission is stated in the material; only the presence of a hostile peer on the network is inferred.

title: The unified compose boots an armed, peer-agnostic admin bypass by default, and separately grants Editor to any authenticated key with public reads on
evidence: `VISIONCLAW_DEV_MODE: "${VISIONCLAW_DEV_MODE:-1}" docker-compose.unified.yml:116 - … ADR-2108 flipped the default from :-0 to :-1 …, so launch.sh up dev boots an ARMED backend and the operator opts OUT` (VC-36.15); `warn banner "VISIONCLAW_DEV_MODE=1 - LAN-LOCAL AUTH BYPASS ACTIVE" project/src/main.rs:296`; `Every request granted as DEV_MODE_PUBKEY = "dev-mode-local-admin" src/utils/auth.rs:96, project/src/main.rs:299`; `LAN-local FULL bypass, peer-agnostic: no NIP-98, no token, no peer check. src/utils/auth.rs:203-218` (VC-36.15); `.env` caveat at project/src/main.rs:109, docker-compose.unified.yml:113-115; release refusal project/src/main.rs:136, :161; `docker-compose.unified.yml:132 sets RBAC_PUBLIC_READS=1 … An unassigned authenticated pubkey resolves to Editor via UserRole::default_authenticated() src/models/rbac.rs:68-70, src/services/role_store.rs:188,196-198` and "two different postures depending whether you read the binary default or the shipped compose env" (VC-33.6); headset LAN target at VC-36.16.

A dev or dev-auth build honours it: `dev_full_bypass_active()` returns true on value `1`, every request is granted as `DEV_MODE_PUBKEY` = "dev-mode-local-admin", and the REST chokepoint path is documented "LAN-local FULL bypass, peer-agnostic: no NIP-98, no token, no peer check" (src/utils/auth.rs:203-218). Release hygiene refuses the variable, but both services load `env_file .env`, "so the var must never sit in a .env shared with prod - sharper now that the compose default supplies it unasked". A service run for a client engagement on this compose therefore grants full admin — settings writes (fanned to every viewer via `settingsUpdated`), physics and graph writes, drag/pin — to anyone who can reach it; the documented headset rig already points at a LAN backend (`XR_BACKEND_WS=ws://192.168.2.132`). confidence: high for the documented mechanism; inferred that a dev-profile service was reachable outside the trusted rail when the incident occurred.

title: Payment replay across processes: the single-use token cache is memory-only and per-process
evidence: "the cache does not span restarts or replicas" and "A freshly signed retry can still repeat an operation" and "Separate storage commits … remain open" (VC-55, developer and business notes); claim under mutex, bounded process-local cache (`nip98.rs:227`, `nip98.rs:295`); durable ledger debit (`pay_handler.rs:303`); effects at `pay_handler.rs:613,686,776,816,862`; verification order VERIFY → CLAIM → EFFECT (VC-55.1 diagram).
failure: a client's signed payment request is verified (signature, freshness, method, URL, body policy) and its signed id claimed under a mutex in a bounded, process-local cache; the operation (sell, swap, pool swap, liquidity) or the resource-fee ledger debit then executes against durable storage. When the service runs as more than one replica, or restarts during a rollout, the replay guard's state is gone: the same captured or client-retried request verifies again on a process whose cache has no record, and the operation or debit executes a second time while only the effects are durable. Independently, even in-process, a client retry that re-signs repeats the operation — there is no idempotency key binding retries — and the material records that auth-spend and effect commit in separate stores.
confidence: high — the cache limitation is stated verbatim; the multi-replica/restart deployment that realises it is inferred (the material does not state the replica count).

title: Any verified identity can join any presence room: no membership gate, no cap, no session recheck
evidence: identity checks then legacy parse (`presence_handler.rs:210,240,249,266,273`); get-or-create and JoinRoom (`presence_handler.rs:281,290,305,306`); duplicate-only rejection (`room.rs:42,45`); member/subscriber insert (`room.rs:51,52`; `presence_actor.rs:681`); parser accepts sha256-12 suffix only (`types.rs:43,48,52` — visionclaw-xr-presence); "no membership gate or cap" (VC-49.1, What it shows); "the 90-second presence deadline still needs implementation" (VC-49.3); business line: restricting a space "requires a separate authority check, durable replay protection and removal handling".
failure: an attacker creates their own DID (identity checks pass for any valid keypair: challenge, signature, verified DID, replay). They send a join for a client's legacy room URN; the parser accepts any sha256-12 suffix; the handler gets-or-creates the actor and sends JoinRoom with the verified DID; the aggregate rejects only duplicate DIDs, then inserts the member and subscriber. There is no membership gate, no cap, and no recheck: the attacker remains a subscriber receiving the room's presence events (membership at minimum; the material does not enumerate the payload) until they choose to disconnect, because the recheck/close path and the 90-second presence deadline are proposals with no implementation.
confidence: high that the gate, cap and recheck are absent (stated); inferred that this path was the incident's vector — which room and what data were exposed is not in evidence.

title: The XR client cannot satisfy the release upgrade gates: production either refuses XR or runs with the gates relaxed
evidence: transport opens with URL (`transport.rs:95`); authenticate only after upgrade (`transport.rs:99,115,118`); release Origin requirement (`http_handler.rs:67,129,131,139`); signed subprotocol/bearer at upgrade (`http_handler.rs:146,151,181,183`); refusal (`http_handler.rs:314,321,322`); "A secret used for the post-upgrade text message cannot satisfy earlier release Origin and authentication checks" and "does not test a deployed proxy or permissive development mode" (VC-48.1); Tension recorded against ADR-2161's Origin prerequisite.
failure: the XR client opens the socket with a URL string and defers authentication to a post-upgrade text message; the release server requires an Origin header plus a signed subprotocol or legacy bearer at upgrade time and refuses the upgrade otherwise. In a correctly configured release deployment, every XR connection is therefore denied (loss of the XR product). The alternative operators have is the permissive development mode or a permissive proxy fronting the endpoint — both explicitly untested in the material. If gates were relaxed or the proxy was permissive to make XR work, upgrades are then admitted without upgrade-time authentication, and the topology and position streams behind them are exposed to any peer that can reach the endpoint.
confidence: medium — the misalignment is stated; which branch production took (refusal vs relaxed configuration) is inferred.
